text:
aisha: heads-up — noticed a regression when enabling rematerialization on long sequences (8k). p99 token latency on the 4-GPU pp/tp config jumped ~28%. attaching a quick profile dump, can anyone eyeball where the extra time is going? :thinking:

ben: can you paste the perf snippet? is this on dedicated infra or local repro?

caroline: fwiw we've seen remat move work from memory to compute and that can disturb overlap with NCCL. might be more frequent smaller allreduces.

Aisha: repro is on dedicated staging (2xTP x2PP, A100s). quick excerpt from nvprof-like sampler: 

```
sample 1: forward matmul  12.3ms  | backward matmul  18.9ms
nvccalls: allreduce  9.7ms (20 calls) | allreduce  2.1ms (80 calls)
KV-cache update RPC: 0.8ms per shard
total step: 128.9ms -> 164.7ms (remat enabled)
```

caroline: that pattern screams "remat causes more fragmented grad syncs". 20 big allreduces replaced by many smaller ones (80). overhead per-call dominates.

diego: can we check whether kernel selection changed? remat sometimes forces smaller matmuls or changes conv->gemm path which impacts compute/comm ratio.

aisha: good call. here's the kernel routing table diff from the run with remat disabled vs enabled (summarized): 
- no-remat: fused-gemm path used for attention (prefers cublasLt), large matmuls batched
- remat: split matmuls, fell back to generic kernel for some leftovers, more kernel launches

ben: falling back to generic kernels + more launches = worse compute density per GPU-op -> less overlap with allreduce. the math checks out.

evan: also check KV-cache behavior: if remat delays when we populate KV cache or forces more frequent cache miss/repush, that can add small RPCs that interleave with allreduce. did the trace show extra KV push events?

aisha: yes, I see extra "kv_push_shard" events right after recompute blocks, roughly correlated with the smaller allreduces.

caroline: short-term mitigation: increase allreduce fusion window (coalesce) on the runtime so multiple small grads are combined before nccl::AllReduce. Have we got a flag? I think runtime has --allreduce-coalesce-us or similar.

diego: runtime flag is `--comm.coalesce_us`. try bumping from 50us to 500us for the repro and re-run. should reduce number of calls but may increase latency tail if we wait too long.

ben: other knob: adjust checkpoint placement to avoid splitting the layer such that the recompute spans PP boundary. aligning checkpoints to pipeline stage boundaries reduces cross-stage micro-syncs.

aisha: plan: 1) run with coalesce=500us 2) run with remat but align checkpoint points to stage boundaries 3) force kernel routing preference for fused matmul path and measure. I'll run 1 and 3 today and post results.

evan: add a microbench: `bench_remat_kv.py --pp 2 --tp 2 --seq 8192 --batch 4 --coalesce 500 --force-kernel fused` — capture nccl_stats and cpu timers.

perf-bot: queued job 3421 for bench_remat_kv.py on staging-gang-7. ETA ~12m. logs will be at https://ci.redwood/3421

caroline: if 1) helps a lot, we should add an adaptive coalescing heuristic: ramp coalesce_us when remat is detected or when allreduce microbursting rises. also consider a compile-time pass that tries to reorder recompute to preserve larger grad chunks.

ben: note: we must watch mempressure — longer coalescing may increase peak GPU memory if we buffer gradients. but for these long sequences we probably have headroom.

diego: small experiment idea: run same config but with KV-cache warmup disabled to confirm RPCs contribute. `--kv.cache_warmup=false`

aisha: thanks. results from job 3421: 

```
no-change (remat + default): step=165ms p99 token latency +28%
with coalesce=500us: step=137ms p99 +6%
with coalesce + force fused kernel: step=122ms p99 ~baseline
nccl stats: num_calls down from 80->22, avg_call_latency up slightly, total_nccl_time down 31%
kv rpc count: down 30% with merged pushes
```

caroline: that's promising — coalescing buys most of it, kernel forcing recovers the rest. sounds like a good short-term patch.

ben: next: add a small perf test to CI that exercises remat on long seqs and fails if allreduce calls > threshold. we'll prevent regressions.

evan: also capture flamegraphs; I'm curious if recompute introduced new hotspots in the runtime scheduler (CPU side) due to finer-grained task submission.

aisha: noted. filing a follow-up issue with notes and repro commands. tagging infra to roll the coalesce bump to staging for a few days.

diego: long-term: compiler/layout strategies to minimize fragmentation of gradient tensors and to prefer kernel paths that maximize compute/comm overlap. also consider a remat-aware comm planner.

aisha: agreed. thanks all. I'll update the issue with perf traces and the recommended runtime flags. :thumbsup:
